entries.title: Amazon loses 40 Leo satellites after ULA's Vulcan rocket fails 10 minutes into flight, marking the first mission failure for the Boeing-Lockheed joint venture (Joey Roulette/Reuters)
Analysis: Huawei's Horinger data center, among China's largest for AI, has ~7% of the compute of SpaceX's Colossus 2 and may stay far behind until at least 2028 (Ben Cottier/Epoch AI)
Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in August 2025 and has no current role, and that it runs a "legitimate and lawful business" as it opens an internal probe (Associated Press)
Sources: Jensen Huang has discussed a comeback as Nvidia CEO with confidants, as allies form a "war room" to lobby for his return and seek White House support (Financial Times)
Sources: Nvidia appealed to Taiwanese officials after its manager was charged over chip smuggling, and sought advice from TSMC, which declined to get involved (Mackenzie Hawkins/Bloomberg)
The US and Pax Silica allies, including Japan, the UK, and India, agree to create a joint list of AI technologies and supply chains to protect from China (Financial Times)
Sources: Howard Lutnick is expected to join Trump on Air Force One to China this week, after clashing with Scott Bessent and others over Nvidia chip curbs (Ashley Gold/Semafor)
Sources: Apple plans to unveil smart glasses at WWDC and ship them by the end of 2027, focusing heavily on integration of third-party iPhone apps with Siri AI (Mark Gurman/Bloomberg)
Investigation: Howard Lutnick pushed to narrow chip curbs affecting a client of his former firm Cantor Fitzgerald whose Malaysia data center may serve Tencent (New York Times)
Scott Bessent urges Nvidia to hire an outside CEO and wants answers within 10 days on whether it pushed "seemingly illicit" chip sales to China to boost revenue (Tony Czuczka/Bloomberg)
Inside the first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles, featuring AI announcers, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins, as the ceremony was mired in technical issues (Corbin Bolies/Variety)
A post-Jensen Nvidia must reshuffle its leadership, reset its DC ties, and recognize that even the US' most valuable company cannot dictate US foreign policy (Chris Miller/Financial Times)
Nidus, which is developing AI-powered tech for manufacturing robots used by US defense industrial companies, raised $30M across a pre-seed and a seed (Alex Konrad/Upstarts Media)
TSMC plans to set up a new $500M fund to invest in chip startups, suppliers, and other upstream partners, saying "we also want to support the future's Nvidia" (Cheng Ting-Fang/Nikkei Asia)
Nebuly, whose tech helps enterprises measure the business value of AI agents by analyzing their impact on productivity and revenue, raised a $21M Series A (Tamara Djurickovic/Tech.eu)
